headword: {専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}

definitions.explanation: A man who does not work outside the home and instead takes care of household duties and childcare full-time.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}をしている。
{妻|つま}の{転勤|てんきん}をきっかけに{専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}になった。
examples.english: I became a stay-at-home dad after my wife's job transfer.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}を{選|えら}ぶ{男性|だんせい}も{増|ふ}えてきたが、まだ{社会的|しゃかいてき}な{理解|りかい}が{十分|じゅうぶん}とは{言|い}えない。
examples.english: More men are choosing to be stay-at-home dads recently, but social understanding is still not enough.

notes:
Composed of {専業|せんぎょう} (full-time, exclusive occupation) + {主夫|しゅふ} (househusband). A relatively modern term that mirrors {専業主婦|せんぎょうしゅふ} (full-time housewife). The kanji {夫|ふ} (husband) distinguishes it from {婦|ふ} (wife). Both words are read せんぎょうしゅふ, so the kanji is needed to tell them apart.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}になる: to become a stay-at-home dad
- {専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}をしている: to be a stay-at-home dad
- {専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ}の{生活|せいかつ}: life as a househusband

CULTURAL NOTE:
While still uncommon in Japan, the number of {専業主夫|せんぎょうしゅふ} has been gradually increasing. The concept has gained visibility through TV dramas and media coverage, though men in this role may still face social stigma.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {専業主婦|せんぎょうしゅふ}: full-time housewife — the female equivalent
- {主夫|しゅふ}: househusband — without {専業|せんぎょう}, may include part-time workers
- イクメン: active father, hands-on dad — a father who is involved in childcare but may still work
